title: These are the asteroids to worry about
beats: Chelyabinsk 2013: asteroid explodes, silent for 90 s, then the shockwave breaks windows
Embarrassment: scientists predicted Duende the same day but missed Chelyabinsk entirely
Only 5 of 1200+ meter-size impactors since 1988 detected; three questions: why hard to detect, chances of a big one, what could we do
Origin of asteroids: protoplanets, heavy cores sink, collisions make rubble piles and iron fragments
Finding asteroids: blink pictures and look for a moving dot against fixed stars
Small, dark (15% reflectivity), so best seen opposite the sun; 85% found in that 45 degrees; Chelyabinsk came from sun side
Detected is not predictable: short arcs are uncertain and dynamical chaos limits prediction to about 100 years
Barringer crater: miner spent 27 years drilling for an iron meteorite that vaporized on impact; impact is explosive, like a nuclear blast, 600x Hiroshima
10 km impactor: debris re-enters worldwide, sky becomes a toaster oven that cooks the surface
Risk arithmetic: one in 100 million per year, so one in a million lifetime; known orbits make it zero
Size ladder: a thousand 1 km rocks per 10 km rock; country-scale damage; 98% found; the unfound 100-800 m ones are the real threat
Can we do anything? Expert says No
Deflection ideas each fail: bomb (rubble reforms), rocket push, laser ablation, aluminum foil wrap
Plain verdict: no way to deflect a 1 km asteroid; 10 km is a thousand times more hopeless
Last resort, evacuate the city: freeways block on the first breakdown
Conclusion: do what we can, survey and build space telescopes, then focus on any dangerous one
Pointer to Domain of Science map of other catastrophes
KiwiCo sponsor read with son; perpetual calendar tied back to asteroid impacts

theory: The video turns a scary topic into a structured set of three questions and answers each with progressively more honest uncertainty. Its strongest teaching move is making the expert fail out loud: every deflection idea collapses, so the viewer arrives at the real recommendation by elimination. Stories (Barringer) carry physics that equations would otherwise carry.
velocity: Orchestrator: support an honest 'we can't' beat; the tutor should be allowed to state unsolved limits plainly.
Scene builder: ladder scene where options appear and are crossed out with a reason, converging on the remaining one.
Learner model: risk-arithmetic items (per-year probability times lifetime) are quizzable, conditioned on new evidence.
Voice: pacing is flat; vary idea density rather than speech rate when a counterintuitive fact lands (opposition effect).
Evals: check that a lesson states the roadmap questions and then answers them in order.
quote: we do not have a way now to deflect a kilometer size asteroid, at all
